notice: Editorial fictional reasoning practice. No Army configurations, alarm labels, commands or real equipment performance are represented. Technical review remains pending.

cases.title: A different build failure
cases.symptom: A dummy workload and its service registration exist. The data volume exists too, but the application cannot read it.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Compare the attachment error and effective access of the workload identity
Check only whether the volume name is listed
Recreate the workload before reading the error
steps.feedback: The invented attachment log reports access denied for the workload identity. The expected volume exists and is healthy; this is an access mismatch, not a missing volume.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Create a second volume with another name
Have the access owner correct the specific dummy identity permission under the exercise baseline
Apply a broad administrator role to every workload
steps.feedback: Use the observed access failure and the approved owner/baseline. Do not recreate healthy objects or broaden unrelated permissions.

steps.context: For this final check, assume the owner completed the approved scoped correction. The volume is attached and the application health check now passes.
options: Accept the volume attachment indicator alone
Confirm a workload object exists
Have the intended dummy user complete the application task using its data
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.

cases.title: A build that stopped late
cases.symptom: The dummy workload runs and its data can be read locally, but the service cannot be discovered by a training user.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Recheck the physical storage path first
Compare the registration step log with the expected service entry
Assume the builder completed because the workload runs
steps.feedback: The synthetic log says the final registration step never ran. Local workload and data checks pass. The expected training service entry is absent.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Follow the approved missing-registration recovery step and validate the entry
Recreate the healthy workload and data volume
Disable user authentication to test discovery
steps.feedback: Recover only the incomplete step after confirming the contract. Registration, authentication and the user task are separate checkpoints.

steps.context: Assume the exercise owner completed the approved registration step. The service is now discoverable; sign-in and task completion have not yet been tested.
options: Stop when the entry appears in the directory
Repeat the authorized dummy user task and verify the intended data result
Accept the original builder completion text
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.

cases.title: A route that works one way
cases.symptom: In a fictional network, the expected OSPF adjacency is full and the forward route exists. Requests arrive at the remote application, but replies never return.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Inspect the destination-side return route and reply-path observations
Reset OSPF simply because the application is unreachable
Rebuild the tunnel before examining packets
steps.feedback: The dummy reply-path observation shows no route back to the source network. The approved baseline contains that return path; local application and modeled policy checks pass.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Adjust OSPF area IDs until the symptom changes
Remove all firewall restrictions
Ask the route owner to restore the missing dummy return path with a rollback point
steps.feedback: A healthy adjacency and forward path cannot substitute for a return path. Correct the documented missing dependency, then test the service.

steps.context: Assume the owner restored the approved return route. Both route lookups now succeed. The user service still needs acceptance.
options: Treat FULL adjacency as proof of application success
Verify bidirectional dummy traffic and the original application task
Accept the forward route alone
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.

cases.title: Small tests work, larger tasks fail
cases.symptom: The fictional tunnel and routes are present. Small messages succeed, but a larger dummy product repeatedly fails.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Reinstall the application before checking the path
Compare packet-size and fragmentation observations across the modeled path
Change the OSPF area because a transfer failed
steps.feedback: The invented path test reports a packet-size limit after encapsulation. Small exchanges pass; the large dummy product does not. No interface value or live command is supplied.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Have the network owner validate the documented packet-size baseline and approved scoped correction
Replace every route with a static default
Rebuild the tunnel security profile on speculation
steps.feedback: A test must exercise the failure condition. The next check is packet-size behavior, not an unsupported routing or security change.

steps.context: Assume the owner corrected the modeled path constraint using the exercise baseline. A small test passes again.
options: Run only the same small test
Accept that the tunnel icon is green
Repeat the original larger dummy transfer and confirm receipt/readability
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.

cases.title: Transport accepted, application still fails
cases.symptom: The fictional service owner has confirmed the approved two-way transport test. A training user cannot open an application by name.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Repeat acquisition without checking the accepted transport evidence
Compare name resolution with the approved application reachability test
Increase transmit settings to improve a name lookup
steps.feedback: The synthetic transport acceptance remains valid and the dummy application is reachable through its supplied test endpoint. The name lookup returns no matching record.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Escalate the missing dummy name record to its service owner and preserve the accepted transport baseline
Repoint the terminal because the application name failed
Rebuild all local VMs
steps.feedback: The evidence points to a name-service dependency after transport acceptance. Do not treat every downstream symptom as a satellite fault.

steps.context: Assume the name-service owner restored the approved dummy record. The lookup now returns the expected test endpoint.
options: Have the authorized user open the application by name and complete the intended task
Accept the name record without testing the application
Accept the original acquisition indication alone
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.

cases.title: A local prerequisite blocks acquisition
cases.symptom: An invented terminal has power but no acquisition indication. Its approved exercise checklist calls for checking the local connection path before any transmit/service request.

steps.prompt: Which check best separates the likely causes?
options: Request a transmit setting change before reviewing local checks
Rebuild the downstream application
Inspect the supplied local-path self-test and checklist status
steps.feedback: The invented self-test reports an open local connection path. This is not a real STT alarm label or a procedure; the exercise baseline requires maintainer review before proceeding.

steps.prompt: What is the supported next action?
options: Ask the authorized maintainer to address the documented local-path blocker; keep dependent tasks blocked
Declare the terminal ready because it has power
Bypass the local check and force a transmit test
steps.feedback: Resolve the observed prerequisite within the documented authority. Acquisition afterward is progress, not proof of usable service.

steps.context: Assume the qualified maintainer cleared the dummy local-path fault. The invented acquisition indication appears, but two-way service has not been accepted.
options: Release all application teams immediately
Coordinate authorized two-way transport acceptance, then routing and the dummy user task
Use the acquisition indication as final acceptance
steps.feedback: Re-test the original user task after the prerequisite checks. A status indicator alone is not end-to-end acceptance.
